question_text: How do two-component systems and phosphorelays transduce signals into transcriptional output?
cutoff_rationale: Largest candidate pool swept so far (19,745, vs. 4,575-6,898 for glmp-q3/q4/q6) -- two-component systems and quorum sensing are both large, well-studied fields. Title-sampling found unambiguous on-topic content through ~p28, then a real mixed zone (false positives from 'component'/'system' as chemistry/physics homonyms -- multicomponent reactions, Turing systems, supramolecular hydrogels) with genuine TCS/QS content still frequent through ~p62. Majority on-topic ends at p62 (score 0.2721), decisively minority from p63 (score 0.2694) onward. Cutoff set at 0.27, between those two.
instrument_note: 'two-component system' hit PubMed esearch's retstart>9998 ceiling (11,257 raw hits, only 9,999 fetched, sorted by relevance so the truncated tail is the least-relevant papers) -- a previously-disclosed instrument limit (GLMP_MASTER_TODO.md item 53's original dry-count), not new to this sweep.
